label: a
rationale: Analysis on R^n with one integration theory underneath, so the same conventions are checked once instead of three times. Batch 7 builds Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space (Caratheodory extension, null sets, Fubini and change of variables); batch 6 proves the divergence theorem and classical Stokes over surface integrals and the total derivative; batch 8's `holomorphic-functions-of-several-variables` declares `fubini-and-change-of-variables`, `the-total-derivative` and `rn-as-a-normed-space` in its own `requires`, and `the-winding-number-and-the-global-cauchy-theorem` is the Green/Stokes-and-cycles argument in the plane. The defects that hide here are shared hypotheses -- piecewise-smooth boundary, orientation sign, measure-zero exceptional sets -- and they are only visible to a reader holding all three pages at once.

label: b
rationale: Combinatorics is the run's only category with two batches and it fits inside one Alpha, so it is not split. The machinery is genuinely common, not merely the category label: batch 5's `linear-algebra-methods-in-combinatorics` is the rank, dimension and eigenvalue toolkit (it requires inner product spaces, Gaussian elimination and polynomial rings), and batch 10's `sparse-restricted-subgraphs-and-rodl-nikiforov` runs exactly that spectral and counting machinery over regular pairs, with `modules-substitution-and-prime-graphs` the structural side of the same graph theory. Batch 5's lattice-path and Catalan bijections also fix the counting conventions batch 10's density statements are stated in.

label: c
rationale: One polynomial-ring and finite-field machinery running through all three. Batch 3 develops finite fields and cyclotomic extensions; batch 1's Lagrange four-square proof turns on `lem-four-square-congruence-for-primes`, the pigeonhole count of squares in F_p that batch 3 formalises, and then on descent by least absolute residues; batch 4's Hilbert basis theorem is a statement about polynomial rings over a Noetherian ring and declares `symmetric-polynomials` and `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`. The same Alpha therefore verifies the F_p square-counting argument once and the polynomial-ring conventions once, rather than meeting each twice in unrelated contexts.

label: d
rationale: The forced pairing, stated as such: nine categories over the available Alphas leaves two singletons sharing, and these two have the most machinery in common. Batch 2 builds central products through an explicit universal property (`thm-universal-property-of-the-central-product`, the antidiagonal central subgroup, `thm-recognition-of-an-internal-central-product`), and batch 9 is ends, coends and weighted limits -- the universal-property and (co)limit calculus itself; one reader checks one notion of universal property and one recognition-by-quotient pattern twice rather than two unrelated ones. Load is the tiebreak: batch 2 is the run's largest single batch at 141 items, so it is paired with a middle-sized batch and kept away from batch 5.
